record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given a red-blue bipartite graph G = (R, B, E) and a positive integer k, is there a nonempty subset R′ of the red side R with at most k vertices such that every vertex in B has an even number of neighbors in R′? Equivalently, is there a nonzero vector x over GF(2) with at most k nonzero coordinates satisfying A x = 0 for the corresponding binary matrix representation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (R ∪ B, E) be a finite undirected bipartite graph with vertex bipartition into a "red" side R and a "blue" side B, and let k be a positive integer. Decide whether there exists a nonempty subset R' ⊆ R with |R'| ≤ k such that every vertex b ∈ B has an even number of neighbors in R' (where 0 counts as even).

Equivalently, given a matrix A over the two-element field GF(2) and a positive integer k, decide whether there exists a nonzero vector x ∈ GF(2)^n with Hamming weight at most k such that Ax = 0.

Parameterized by k, is this decision problem fixed-parameter tractable? That is, does there exist an algorithm solving it in time f(k)·|input|^{O(1)} for some computable function f?
artifact.status_search_result: The k-Even Set problem has been shown to be W[1]-hard under randomized reductions by Bhattacharyya, Bonnet, Egri, Ghoshal, Karthik C. S., Lin, Manurangsi, and Marx (2019, "Parameterized Intractability of Even Set and Shortest Vector Problem"). This provides strong evidence against fixed-parameter tractability, but whether k-Even Set is in FPT under deterministic reductions remains formally open.

status_evidence.title: Parameterized Intractability of Even Set and Shortest Vector Problem
status_evidence.snippet: k-Even Set is W[1]-hard under randomized reductions; rules out FPT approximation with any constant ratio.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is W[1]-hard under randomized reductions, giving strong evidence it is not FPT, though the deterministic FPT question is not fully resolved.
